section_title: Why does the elder hope to speak face to face?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 12 I have many things to write to you, but I would prefer not to do so with paper and ink. Instead, I hope to come and speak with you face to face, so that our joy may be complete. 13 The children of your elect sister send you greetings.

context_lines: The elder has more to say, but he hopes to visit and speak face to face so that their shared joy may be complete. The letter gives what is needed now while looking toward a fuller personal conversation.
The closing greeting comes from the children of the elect sister. It echoes the opening address and ends the letter with a relationship between the people sending and receiving it.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-second-epistle-of-st-john/) reads the greeting in terms of an actual sister’s children; the [USCCB note](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/2john/1) reads it as a greeting between churches. Both recognize the desire for personal conversation. Neither the wording here nor the reference to paper and ink states that persecution is the reason for postponing the rest.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
